findings.F1: In the thin-volume regime (28-day mean volume below the prior year's, the recorded "trending" regime), a coin's raw 28-day return predicts its 10-day excess return with the same sign: slope 0.144, t 2.49 clustered by day (342 cases, 90 days); measured in units of the coin's 20-day daily volatility, the slope's t is 2.75. Outside the regime the slope is -0.034, t -0.82 (263 cases).
findings.F2: Inside the thin-volume regime the effect runs on both sides and is graded. The lowest 28-day-return quintile was followed by -4.98 % excess over 10 days (t -4.07, 71 cases), and the highest by +5.75 % (t 2.00, 69 cases). Taken separately, falls give slope 0.23 (t 1.47, 184 cases) and rises slope 0.18 (t 1.48, 158 cases).
findings.F3: The thin-volume slope on the 28-day return is positive for all 6 coins (BTC t 2.05, ETH t 1.96, ZEC t 1.68, XMR t 1.14, XRP t 1.14, LTC t 0.89). It is positive in 2019 to 2021 but negative in 2018 (-0.16, t -0.87). At a 5-day horizon it holds too: slope 0.075, t 2.59 (684 cases, 181 days).
findings.F4: The tested forecast, the 28-day change standardised over 60 bars and clipped at 0, correlates only 0.72 with the raw 28-day return on thin fallen bars. Its own slope t is 1.60 (241 cases), against 2.75 for the volatility-scaled 28-day return. The verdict's inconclusive t of 0.68 partly reflects this transform, not only the idea.
findings.F5: A large one-day fall tends to be followed by a rebound the next day, but the evidence is weaker than the raw numbers suggest. The day after the lowest quintile of one-day return scaled by 20-day volatility gained +0.66 % excess (t 4.34, 1392 bars). That t is not clustered by day, so cases on several coins the same day inflate it. With clustering, the graded slope is negative in all 4 years (t -1.75, -0.82, -1.88, -0.53) and for 5 of 6 coins (XMR t -3.56, ETH t -2.43).
findings.F6: Among fallen coins (28-day return below 0), a narrow recent range was followed by a rebound rather than a further fall, against the brief. The lowest quintile of 10-day range relative to the 60-day range gained +4.33 % excess over 10 days (t 2.00). The pooled graded slope is only t -1.37 (605 cases, 113 days), so this cannot be told from chance after this many angles.
findings.F7: The book lost 7.3 % a year (Sharpe -0.25) even though the supporting excess was +0.74 %. The coins' normal drift in the short's direction (-1.28 % per 10 days) outweighed the unusual move, so the total move per case (-0.72 %) is negative, at -3.8 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade.

ideas.idea: When a coin's volume over the past 28 days is below its usual volume of the year before, the larger its 28-day return measured against its own daily volatility, the larger its return in the same direction over the next 10 days: thin-volume rises keep rising and thin-volume falls keep falling.
ideas.consequence: In a quiet-volume stretch, a trader should follow the coin's 28-day move, long after rises and short after falls, more strongly the larger the move against its volatility.
ideas.name: thin-volume trend continues

ideas.idea: When a coin's volume over the past 28 days is below its usual volume of the year before, the larger its 28-day rise measured against its own daily volatility, the larger its further rise over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A strong rise on thin volume is a reason to stay long for about ten days, more so the stronger the rise.
ideas.name: quiet rally keeps rising

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's one-day fall measured against its 20-day daily volatility, the larger its rise over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A sharp one-day drop is a reason to refuse a fresh short for the next day, more so the sharper the drop.
ideas.name: sharp daily drop rebounds
